title: Application of Ticket Credit
content:
Ticket credit held on a Lift Tickets order is applied only when it is applied no later than its validity period counted in calendar days from the day the credit was issued. A single application must be at least the product's minimum.

## How the calendar days are counted

Calendar days are counted forward from the anchor date, the anchor date itself counting as day zero, every day of the week counting alike, and a calendar day is never mixed with a full 24-hour period; where the resulting boundary falls on a date that does not exist in the target month, the last day of that month is used.

The anchor date here is the day the credit was issued, as the order's own record of that credit shows it. The comparison is one of not being later: an application falling on the last day of the period is within it, that day being counted inclusively.

## The count worked through

Take a validity period of 20 calendar days and a credit issued on 2027-03-01; both are taken for this illustration, and the period each product actually carries is its own.

- 2027-03-01 is day zero, being the day the credit was issued.
- Counting forward 20 calendar days, weekdays and weekend days alike, the last day of the period is 2027-03-21.
- An application made on 2027-03-21 is not later than the period and stands.
- An application made on 2027-03-22 is later than the period.

Where such a count lands on a date the target month does not have — the 31st of a thirty-day month, say — the last day of that month is used instead.

## The smallest application

Ticket credit is not applied in any amount smaller than the product's minimum for one charge. The amount of credit standing on the order may exceed that minimum many times over; what the rule governs is the size of a single application.
